newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Treasury figures fit NZ Labour's plans - Cullen.
newsitem.headline: Treasury figures fit NZ Labour's plans - Cullen.

text.p: Labour finance spokesman Michael Cullen on Thursday said he was "quietly smiling" over the figures released in the pre-election economic and fiscal update.
"We haven't done all the numbers yet but we don't see we will have any difficulty meeting the bottom line target for debt reduction," Cullen said.

He said Labour was aiming to reduce net debt by two percent of GDP in each of the next three years, and on the basis of Treasury's forecasts Labour would not have to change any of its policy platform.
"We should easily make that target," Cullen said.
He said on balance the update should have no impact on monetary policy, with stronger growth balanced by an improved fiscal position.
"But given the potentially anal-retentive nature of Reserve Bankers around the world, we may assume not a great deal of joy."
He said the Reserve Bank in its economic outlook on Friday should see room to loosen monetary policy, although not immediately.

He said the only major change in the Treasury update from the May Budget night figures was the reduction in the operating surplus for the 1995/96 year from $3.9 billion to $3.31 billion. This was largely explained by a court judgement of $328 million against the Crown over the sale of New Zealand Steel to Equiticorp in 1987 and financing costs from the repurchase of some long-dated foreign currency debt.
